column4: The section develops the night-day succession as a recurring sign and links it with remembrance and gratitude. This verse names the alternation of night and day among signs, alongside rain, winds, and provision, placing the cycle within a larger pattern of sustenance.

The image turns on two alternating times. This verse names the variation of night and day as a sign for people of understanding, extending the source's daily scene into reflection on the created order.
The section treats the regular change between night and day as purposeful. This verse calls their alternation, together with creation in the heavens and earth, a sign for the mindful.

The source links the recurring night-day sequence to remembrance and gratitude. This verse places night-day variation beside rain and the changing winds as signs, relating the cycle to provision from the sky and earth.

The section pairs duha and settled night as two phases of a regular order. This verse names the sun and moon's continuing courses and says night and day are made serviceable, joining the image's lights and times to provision.

The source stages sunlight, night, and their succession. This verse groups night and day with the sun, moon, and stars, all made subject to God's command, presenting the same celestial scene as an ordered sign.

The section's night is a covering and repose, not an ending or abandonment. This verse speaks of God taking people at night, knowing their daytime acts, then raising them by day; it makes the night's covering temporary within an ongoing relation to God.
